document_summary: Requirements document for a provider self-service portal to allow healthcare providers to manage their profile information, upload credentialing documents, view network status and payment history. Project was drafted in 2023 but deprioritized in favor of Rules Engine migration.

entities.name: Provider Self-Service Portal
entities.description: Self-service web portal for healthcare providers to manage their information and interact with Clearview
entities.overview: A proposed provider-facing web portal that would allow healthcare providers to update demographic information, upload credentialing documents, view network participation status, and access payment history. The system was designed to reduce manual processing workload for the Provider Network team by enabling provider self-service.
entities.details: The Provider Portal would serve as the primary interface for Clearview's 14K+ contracted providers to manage their relationship with the health plan. Core functionality includes profile management (address, phone, practice locations), credentialing document upload (medical license, DEA certificate, malpractice insurance), network status viewing, fee schedule access, and payment history with ERA 835 download capability. The system would implement role-based access control with FIDO2/WebAuthn authentication and integrate with Provider Directory, Payment Engine, and potentially Pre-Auth Service. The project was originally planned for 2024 delivery but was paused in December 2023 due to Rules Engine migration priority, with potential restart in Q1 2026.

entities.name: Provider Office Manager
entities.description: Primary user persona for Provider Portal - handles administrative tasks at provider offices
entities.overview: The main user of the Provider Portal who manages credentials, updates practice information, and checks payment status. This persona represents the administrative staff at healthcare provider offices who handle the business operations and interact with health plans on behalf of the providers.
entities.details: Provider Office Managers are the primary target users for the Provider Portal, responsible for managing provider demographic information, uploading credentialing documents, monitoring network participation status, accessing fee schedules, and tracking payment history. They handle the day-to-day administrative interactions with Clearview and would be the most frequent users of the portal's functionality. In the current manual process, they email or fax changes to the Provider Network team.

relationships.reasoning: Identified as the primary user persona for the portal

entities.reasoning: Explicitly defined as the primary user persona with clear responsibilities

entities.name: Clearview Provider Relations Rep
entities.description: Internal user who reviews and approves provider-submitted changes through the portal
entities.overview: Internal Clearview employee responsible for reviewing provider-submitted changes and acting as a gatekeeper for sensitive modifications. This role ensures data quality and prevents unauthorized changes to critical provider information.
entities.details: Provider Relations Representatives are internal Clearview users who would review and approve provider-submitted changes through the portal, particularly for sensitive data like address and phone number updates. They serve as gatekeepers for changes that could impact provider payments or network participation. The requirement specifies they should review changes within 2 business days. They would have administrative access to approve or reject provider submissions.

relationships.reasoning: Internal user who reviews provider submissions through the portal

entities.reasoning: Clearly defined as an internal user role with specific approval responsibilities

entities.name: Credentialing Specialist
entities.description: Internal user who reviews credentialing document submissions and manages re-credentialing workflows
entities.overview: Internal Clearview employee specialized in credentialing processes who reviews provider-uploaded documents and manages the re-credentialing workflow. This role ensures providers maintain proper credentials and comply with NCQA requirements.
entities.details: Credentialing Specialists are internal users who would be notified when providers upload new credentialing documents through the portal. They review medical licenses, DEA certificates, malpractice insurance, board certifications, and CME records to ensure provider compliance. They manage the re-credentialing workflow and monitor credential expiration dates, with system alerts sent 90 days before expiration per NCQA requirements for 3-year re-credentialing cycles.

relationships.reasoning: Reviews credentialing documents submitted through the portal

entities.reasoning: Explicitly defined as internal user role with credentialing-specific responsibilities

entities.name: Provider Change Approval Workflow
entities.description: Two-business-day approval process for provider demographic changes submitted through the portal
entities.overview: A workflow process where Provider Relations Representatives review and approve provider-submitted changes to demographic information within 2 business days. This process ensures data quality while enabling provider self-service for non-critical updates.
entities.details: When providers submit changes to address, phone, fax, email, office hours, or accepting-new-patients status through the portal, these changes enter an approval queue for Provider Relations review. The process has a 2-business-day SLA for review and approval. Once approved, changes are pushed to the Provider Directory in real-time. Sensitive changes like NPI, TIN, specialty, and credentials require manual review and cannot be self-updated through the portal.

relationships.reasoning: Portal would implement this approval workflow
Provider Relations Rep performs the approval review

entities.reasoning: Clearly described workflow with specific SLA and approval requirements

entities.name: Credentialing Document Workflow
entities.description: Process for providers to upload credentialing documents and specialists to review them
entities.overview: A workflow enabling providers to upload credentialing documents through the portal, with automatic notification to Credentialing Specialists for review. The process tracks credentialing status and provides automated expiration alerts.
entities.details: Providers can upload medical licenses, DEA certificates, malpractice insurance, board certifications, and CME records in PDF, JPG, or PNG format (max 10MB per file). Documents are stored in a secure document management system and Credentialing Specialists are automatically notified of new uploads. The system tracks credentialing status (ACTIVE, PENDING, EXPIRED, REVIEW_REQUIRED) and sends alerts 90 days before credential expiration to comply with NCQA requirements for 3-year re-credentialing cycles.

entities.name: Provider Portal Backend-for-Frontend
entities.description: Proposed BFF API to serve the Provider Portal frontend with provider-specific data aggregation
entities.overview: A proposed Backend-for-Frontend service that would aggregate data from multiple backend services (Provider Directory, Payment Engine, Pre-Auth Service) to serve the Provider Portal frontend. This architectural approach would separate provider-facing API concerns from internal system APIs.
entities.details: James Whitfield prefers building a separate BFF rather than extending the existing Provider Directory API with provider-facing endpoints, to avoid mixing internal and external API concerns. The BFF would handle authentication, authorization, and data aggregation from Provider Directory for profile data, Payment Engine for payment history and ERA 835 access, and potentially Pre-Auth Service for prior authorization submission. The service would implement role-based access control and handle the provider-specific data formatting and security requirements.

entities.overview: A data model that tracks provider credentialing status through defined status values: ACTIVE, PENDING, EXPIRED, and REVIEW_REQUIRED. The model supports the credentialing workflow and compliance monitoring requirements.
entities.details: The credentialing status model includes status enumeration (ACTIVE, PENDING, EXPIRED, REVIEW_REQUIRED) and likely includes expiration dates for tracking 90-day alert requirements. The model supports NCQA compliance requirements for 3-year re-credentialing cycles and integrates with the automated alert system for credential expiration notifications.

entities.name: Provider Data Update Restrictions
entities.description: Business rules defining which provider data fields can be self-updated versus requiring manual review
entities.overview: Business rules that govern which provider information can be self-updated through the portal versus requiring manual review for data integrity and compliance. These rules balance provider self-service convenience with data security and accuracy requirements.
entities.details: Providers can self-update: address, phone, fax, email, office hours, accepting-new-patients flag, and practice locations (add, remove, edit). Providers CANNOT self-update: NPI, TIN, specialty, and credentials - these require manual review due to their critical nature for payment processing, network management, and credentialing compliance. Address and phone changes go through a 2-business-day approval queue handled by Provider Relations representatives to ensure accuracy.

entities.reasoning: Clearly specified business rules with explicit allowed and restricted fields

entities.name: Credential Expiration Alert Rules
entities.description: Business rule requiring 90-day advance alerts for credential expiration per NCQA requirements
entities.overview: Automated alert system that notifies providers 90 days before credential expiration to ensure compliance with NCQA requirements for 3-year re-credentialing cycles. This rule supports proactive credential management and regulatory compliance.
entities.details: The system must alert providers 90 days before credential expiration to comply with NCQA requirements for re-credentialing every 3 years. This includes medical licenses, DEA certificates, malpractice insurance, board certifications, and CME records. The alert system would be automated and integrated with the credentialing status tracking to ensure providers have adequate time to renew credentials before expiration.

relationships.reasoning: Portal would implement the automated alert system

entities.reasoning: Specific regulatory requirement with clear 90-day alert timeframe and NCQA compliance purpose

entities.name: Provider Portal Deprioritization (2023)
entities.description: Decision to pause Provider Portal development in December 2023 in favor of Rules Engine migration
entities.overview: Strategic decision made in December 2023 to deprioritize the Provider Portal project in favor of the Rules Engine migration. The project was originally planned for 2024 delivery but was paused with potential restart in Q1 2026.
entities.details: The Provider Portal project was paused in December 2023 despite having requirements documented and timeline planned for Q1-Q4 2024 delivery. The decision was made to prioritize the Rules Engine migration project over provider portal development. As of October 2025, the project is tentatively scheduled for Q1 2026 roadmap, with James re-validating requirements. This decision reflects the strategic importance of the Rules Engine migration and limited development resources.

relationships.reasoning: Decision directly affected the Provider Portal project timeline
Provider Network team made the prioritization decision

entities.reasoning: Clearly documented decision with timeline and reasoning provided in the document
